Method of Attack: Encrypts victim's data files using AES-256 encryption
Encrypts file names and appends random 4-digit extension
Stops specific processes to encrypt associated files
Scans and encrypts files on unmapped Windows shares if network setting enabled
Deletes Shadow Volume Copies to prevent recovery
Creates ransom notes with instructions and links to Tor payment site
Uses VBScript to speak ransom message to victim
Installs itself in %AppData% folder with random executable name
Configures Windows to boot into Safe Mode with Networking on reboot
Displays fake system alerts and forces restart
Impacted Systems: Systems excluding certain CIS countries (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan)
Attack Vector: Offered as Ransomware as a Service (RaaS) on closed underground Russian forum
Indicators of Compromise: Ransom note files: # DECRYPT MY FILES #.html, # DECRYPT MY FILES #.txt, # DECRYPT MY FILES #.vbs, Readme.hta
Registry entries under HKCU with path %AppData%\{2ED2A2FE-872C-D4A0-17AC-E301404F1CBA}\[random].exe
File extensions encrypted including .accdb, .mdb, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .pdf, .jpg, .txt, .zip, and many others
Bitcoin ransom demand of 1.24 bitcoins (~500 USD)
Use of command: C:\Windows\System32\bcdedit.exe /set {current} safeboot network
Use of command: C:\Windows\System32\wbem\WMIC.exe shadowcopy delete
